messages:
maya: FYI, after last night's OOB firmware roll in ap-south1 a subset of BMCs are reporting a partition TTL mismatch. Provisioner is queuing hosts and GPU allocation dropped ~18% :grimacing:
leo: seeing the same. provisioning queue length jumped around 00:12 UTC, GPUs stuck in PENDING for >5m
sam: ops-bot alerted at 00:14. logs show 'kv-partition ttl mismatch' on model 2.1 images on about 24 racks
ops-bot: Automated alert: bmc-monitor detected partition-ttl-drift on 24 nodes in ap-south1. Severity: medium. Affected services: fleet-provisioner, gpu-scheduler. Ticket: https://redwoodops.example/t/INC-8471 :rotating_light:
ana: (sorry hands full) any quick mitigation other than rollback? we have queued Dedicated jobs hitting SLA
jin: can we force re-sync of bmc partition metadata without flash rollback? I have a script to replay NVRAM sync 
leo: try re-sync first. sample command we used in staging: `oob-sync --region ap-south1 --filter kv-ttl --replay`
jin: running it against one rack now, will paste output
jin: ```
2026-03-21T00:42:15Z INFO starting oob-sync rack=rack-az1
2026-03-21T00:42:18Z WARN kv-partition mismatch detected: active_ttl=120 expected_ttl=300
2026-03-21T00:42:20Z INFO replaying partition metadata from control-plane
2026-03-21T00:42:24Z INFO sync complete, ttl normalized to 300
```
sam: good sign. if that fixes, we can schedule a rolling resync across racks during low traffic window
maya: can we estimate cost impact if we pause rollouts and spill workload to other regions? finance flagged potential +12% GPU spend if we do cross-region overflow for 6 hours
leo: rough calc: current committed capacity for Dedicated is 520 GPUs in ap-south1. At 18% reduction that's ~94 GPUs. If we overflow to hosted/dedicated in eu-west/usw1 at on-demand rates expect ~$28k over 6 hours. needs PM approval
ana: I can approve up to $5k emergency spend. beyond that we escalate to product ops and finance
inja: (typo, not in participants)
manual: please ignore
maya: plan: 1) run oob-sync replay across remaining affected racks (in waves of 10) starting 01:15 UTC 2) monitor provisioner backlog 3) only if resync fails for >30m start controlled region overflow 4) postpone any firmware pushes until root cause repro is clear
leo: I'll author a short runbook and post in /runbooks/oob-resync.md after first wave passes
ops-bot: Update: oob-sync succeeded on rack-az1, rack-az2, rack-az3. Provisioner backlog decreased by 47% in 7m
sam: provisioning queue near baseline now. observing a few hosts with WARN but they transition to READY after resync
ana: thanks team. let's keep rollouts paused for the week and add TTL-check to preflight for future firmware pushes
maya: agreed. scheduling postmortem for 09:00 UTC tomorrow. I'll capture logs and add to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
